evidence: Full CDIAL barkara gives regional bakarā/bakrā and feminine bakarī/bakrī goat, plus Garhwali/Kumaoni/Nepali bākhro with aspiration. Selected Tharu bakariya-type responses retain the ordinary expanded feminine ending, and Kului a/schwa plus retroflex-r forms retain their exact articulation and vowel notation. This is the barkara family; rounded forms overlapping bokka are excluded. Local IA transmission remains unresolved.

Full CDIAL bokka explicitly gives Prakrit bokkaḍa goat, Old Gujarati bokaḍaü he-goat and Marathi bokaḍ; it also compares Sanskrit bukka goat and gives Oriya bukā. Selected western Bhil/Bareli bukaḍo/bukəḍi/bukuḍo/bukḍo-type goat forms have the documented stop extension, with ordinary gender/vowel endings retained. The survey generic goat sense is preserved rather than narrowed to male. The u/o variation is qualified; no particular cross-IA donor route or deeper origin of bokka is asserted. Rhotic forms that overlap barkara remain separate.
